summary.headline: Simplex Castings Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 35% YoY to ₹60.95 crore and PAT rose about 45% to ₹6.86 crore, with near-term order book at ~₹150 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹60.95 crore, up about 35% YoY from ₹45.21 crore and up 11% QoQ from ₹54.76 crore. EBITDA rose about 25% YoY to ₹11.52 crore, with margin of 18.89%, and PAT rose about 45% YoY to ₹6.86 crore (PAT margin 11.25% vs 10.48%). Management said the near-term order book has expanded to roughly ₹150 crore+ from a historical ₹80–100 crore range. Management guided to ~₹300 crore FY27 revenue and ~₹500 crore by FY28, and flagged working capital reduction as a FY27 transition priority.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing; management targets more than ₹100 crore next year from railway business, including casted bogies (~200 per month capacity conditional on wagon orders) and fabricated locomotive bogies at Tedesara expected at ₹60–70 crore turnover.

segments.name: Power sector fabrication
segments.commentary: No power/BHL orders in last year; management targets ~₹100 crore from power sector next year via orders secured through RXIL with BHL and L&T.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Mazgaon Dock)
segments.commentary: First order of 5 sets about ₹4.5 crore; 3 sets already cast and first offered for inspection. A further pipeline order is about ₹8 crore.

segments.name: Steel and metallurgical
segments.commentary: Steel is the core market; management says ~₹300 crore of FY27 revenue will be fed by steel sector. Non-ferrous is about 20% of order book.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Target 5–10% of business in FY27 (with shipbuilding, 10–15%), working first with one ordnance factory (Khamaria, Jabalpur); not expected to grow 20–30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance ~₹300 crore; management says ₹60 crore done in Q1 and balance ~₹150 crore order book to be executed in FY27, plus pipeline orders by March.

Revenue target of ~₹500 crore by FY28; management says the current fundraise is sufficient to reach this, and expansion beyond existing two units (~₹300–350 crore capacity) will come via organic or inorganic routes.
Capacity utilisation currently 50–60%, targeted at least 80% by end of FY28.
Working capital: FY27 described as transition year; target operating cycle of 60–70 days by FY28 from about 100–120 days today.
Fabrication capacity expansion of 1,500 tons per month (~18,000 tons annual) versus ~6,000 tons currently being done, implying an addition of 6,000–8,000 tons.
EPC business to be restarted selectively: order sizes ₹100–150 crore, ~2-year execution, minimum margin 15–20%, targeting about ₹100 crore annual revenue, funded from bank limits and accruals.
capex_capacity: Capex in progress at Tedesara (Rajnandgaon) unit, expected to complete in FY27; CWIP about ₹30 crore incl. working capital.
Fabrication expansion: 1,500 tons per month capacity addition, roughly 18,000 tons per year, for power and fabricated bogies.
Foundry is debottlenecking only: one CNC machine at ₹4–5 crore plus conveyors and cranes; machine moulding plant only on drawing board.
Capacity utilisation 50–60% currently; targeted 80% by end FY28.
Future capacity beyond current two units is not yet committed; management says investments will be funded from internal accruals, not new borrowings.
demand_pricing: Order book near-term ~₹150 crore+; management intends to keep it at ₹100–150 crore to limit liquidated damages (typically capped at 5%, some up to 10%).

Working capital: product mix shift at Unit 1 toward fast-moving, shorter-cycle products; Unit 3 to follow. Railway bogie cycle 30–45 days; RXIL and Invoice Mart discounting payments in ~30–35 days after dispatch at ~5–5.5% discount rate.
Steel demand supported by ArcelorMittal expansions (two in Odisha, one in Andhra Pradesh); management says steel boom expected to last 4–5 years.
Non-ferrous and metallurgical (Balco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc, Nalco, Aditya Birla) about 20% of order book.
Competition from Shyam Metalics and Rungta also expanding; management says Simplex is one of few large players in Bhilai.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at roughly 50–60%; targeting at least 80% by end of next financial year, with gradual increase starting this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹60 crore done in Q1, with ~₹150 crore order book to execute in FY27 and pipeline orders to come by March; management said ₹300 crore is in line.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital fall from 60–90 days (or 100–120 days) to target levels, and what is the margin cost of invoice discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to railway bogies (30–45 day cycle, payment upfront from wagon builders) and RXIL/Invoice Mart (30–35 days post dispatch). Discounting costs about 5–5.5%. Management said ₹300 crore revenue would need only about ₹50 crore working capital at 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall as railway and power fabrication (tender-based) grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management conceded railway and power fabrication will be at similar margins to today, not higher; margin uplift will come from selecting more complex, niche products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the fundraise sufficient to reach ₹500 crore, and any further borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current fundraise is sufficient for the ₹500 crore projection; further expansion will be funded only from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Green hydrogen DRI project status?
qa_highlights.answer: Project closed. Grant of ~₹160 crore was subject to GST (~₹30–35 crore) because of IP and asset-sharing conditions; the reissued tender required an operating DRI plant, so Simplex did not bid.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term opportunities beyond ₹500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to detail; areas mentioned include machine tool castings, defence and possible technology JVs or acquisitions; management reiterated no concrete plans yet.

financial_highlights.change: +35% YoY (from ₹45.21 crore); +11% QoQ (from ₹54.76 crore in Q4 FY26)
Deployed in working capital and capex

risks_watch: Execution of the ~₹150 crore order book and pipeline orders by March 2027 is needed to hit the ~₹300 crore FY27 guidance; ₹60 crore is done in Q1.
Railway casted bogies (~200 per month) depend on wagon orders expected August–September; management said capacity ramp will only start once those orders are placed.
Working capital transition: operating cycle is ~100–120 days today versus the 60–70 day FY28 target; management said the improvement will be gradual and may not be fully visible immediately.
Margin mix: management conceded railway and power fabrication will earn margins similar to current levels, not higher; watch whether niche product mix lifts PAT margin.
Green hydrogen DRI project closed after GST issue (~₹30–35 crore) on grant conditions; no commercial opportunity from it going forward.
Capacity beyond the two units (~₹300–350 crore) is uncommitted; the ₹500 crore FY28 target depends on unnamed organic or inorganic pipeline, to be funded from internal accruals.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and FY27 revenue guidance, with repeated caution on timelines for working capital and defence. Management was evasive on specific acquisition, JV and long-term pipeline details, saying these are on the back burner and not yet concrete.

Fabrication capacity addition of 1,500 tons/month (~18,000 tons/yr) vs ~6,000 tons currently done
Foundry debottlenecking: one CNC machine at ₹4-5 crore plus conveyors and cranes

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at ~₹300 crore versus ~₹181 crore run-rate implied by Q1 ₹60.95 crore x4 is not directly comparable, but ₹60 crore done in Q1 and ₹150 crore order book back the guide; Tedesara capex completes in FY27 and utilisation at 50-60% leaves headroom, though the ₹300 crore guide needs a steep ramp in the remaining quarters.
